page: Microsoft Azure F1ams_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine from the Famsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features a single dedicated physical core and vCPU powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor with an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz and includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, but it is premium storage capable.

Benchmark data highlights strong single-core capabilities alongside expected multi-core limitations due to the single-vCPU configuration. The instance achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU testing and single-threaded compression and decompression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3. However, multi-core CPU performance, PassMark CPU scores, and database operations fall into the lower tier. Memory bandwidth for large block read and write operations is average, while small block cached reads are relatively weak. Large-block uncached read speeds reach 42.07 GB/sec, and write speeds reach 31.72 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1ams_v7 offers a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring a high memory-to-vCPU ratio without the need for multi-threaded processing power. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance compared to shared-core burstable instances. This server is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive tasks, single-threaded applications, basic web serving, and small-scale LLM inference tasks using small models.
